finding.mechanism: The predecessor ClayVerse swarm admission assertion returned status PASS when tools/run_go_zero_swarm.py existed without validating that controller. File presence could therefore turn the quarantine assertion green even for a stale or unreviewed controller.
finding.risk: A copied/renamed legacy Mini Entity controller could bypass the intended source-level quarantine signal and recreate product-authority drift before a real ClayVerse controller admission contract exists.

delta.rule: CLAYVERSE_SWARM_ADMISSION_ASSERTION/v2 is quarantine-only. Any current-controller file fails closed with CURRENT_CONTROLLER_PRESENT_REQUIRES_SEPARATE_VALIDATION until a separately reviewed versioned controller validator explicitly replaces this contract.

poison_cases: legacy Mini Entity controller copied to tools/run_go_zero_swarm.py -> FAIL_CLOSED
arbitrary ClayVerse-named candidate at tools/run_go_zero_swarm.py -> FAIL_CLOSED
bootstrap product regressed to Mini Entity -> FAIL_CLOSED

next_gate: Merge only as source-level fail-closed hardening after current-main compatibility review. A future provider swarm remains blocked until a real ClayVerse controller and a separately versioned deterministic controller admission validator exist and execute before secret lookup/network I/O.
